architecture.mechanism: Distributed energy-storage architecture composed of many individual cells with separate ancillary monitoring and control, where per-cell degradation rates (rather than a single lumped battery state) determine system behavior and are tracked to anticipate failure.
architecture.intervention: Replace the single 12V battery with a distributed low-voltage storage bank of multiple independent cell modules, each on its own fused power path to critical safety loads (rear/exterior manual door releases, mechanical locking, emergency communications), and add a per-cell health monitor that tracks individual cell degradation rates so a failing cell is detected and electrically isolated before it takes down the whole low-voltage bus.
architecture.expected_effect: Total failure of any one cell or module no longer disables door releases, locks, or emergency communications, because remaining modules keep the critical loads energized; degradation-driven failures are predicted and isolated in advance instead of occurring as a single-point event.
architecture.falsification_test: In a bench vehicle, force a hard short/dead-short on one 12V cell module and verify with a multimeter and functional test that rear manual door releases, exterior manual releases, mechanical locks, and emergency communications still operate continuously for at least 30 minutes; separately, run accelerated cycling and confirm the per-cell monitor flags the failing module (capacity/resistance trend crossing threshold) at least 50 cycles before it fails.
